source:
I want to build an airship combat game.

# Setting:
Steampunk-styled feudal universe where humanity lives in the clouds and gets around by airship. The justification is that in this universe the atmosphere is denser so airships have an easier time floating. The game takes place in a war being fought between two major kingdoms. The player is a small fiefdom with a battle airship that may be called upon to go to battle in service of their kingdom (analogous to how knights owned castles and were called up in medieval times). The details and lore can be fleshed out after the mechanics are, but this sets the motivation for the gameplay loop

# Gameplay:
The gameplay revolves around large PvE battles in a similar style to helldivers 2. Once matchmaking selects a team of players, there is first a planning phase where the players are all debriefed with "intelligence" relating to what they're up against and where they're fighting (e.g. environmental hazards, cloud/weather cover, force composition, wildlife hazards) and can collaboratively draw up a battle plan. Then the battle begins, and depending on the objective runs to completion. After the battle, the player earns research points and money to research and buy components. They can then build/upgrade their airship and take it to combat

# Main features and open questions:
 ⁃ Damage model: I want this to be dynamic, similar to how war thunder works. For example, if you hit an ammo locker and penetrate, it should really destroy some components. Similarly, if you hit the air bag of a ship, it should start to very slowly lose lift. Naturally everyone is going to be shooting for the air bags because of this, but as in real life the egress of lift gas is very low and in this game unlike in real life it isn't flammable. You'd have to really get shredded or rammed for it to start to be a rapid issue
 ⁃ Combat Styles:
 ⁃ Classic: Similar to how ship combat is set up in world of warships or the war thunder Bluewater navies mode, but in 3d. 
 ⁃ Team: Similar to how ship combat is in sea of thieves
 ⁃ Game Modes:
 ⁃ PvP (Skirmish): Classic pvp with a ticket system, following the war thunder arcade mode formula. This mode will filter out the players that don't care about the team tactics/strategic element of the game. These battles do not affect the "world state"
 ⁃ PvE (War): Similar in idea to helldivers 2 battles, which are PvE and the outcome of which impacts the overall state of the world, and starwars battlefront's multi-stage battles where the objectives change over time. My idea is that at the start of the battle the players get debriefed and can collaborate on a rough battle plan. I'm not sure the most fun way to implement this, so some research is required as to examples of similar mechanics in other games and how they have been received. For example, what is the best way to allow visual collaboration? I imagine we need both the ability to draw up attack/defense plans, and to group players on the same team by objective (e.g. you two go attack their left flank, then during the battle the LLM orchestrating the execution of the plan presents the corresponding objective to those two players). Once the battle begins the players see objectives based on the plan selected, which should change dynamically as combat progresses. I imagine that it would be neat to create an API/MCP for setting the dynamic objectives, and using two LMaaS agents (one for the player team and one for the enemy team) to act as strategic commanders and issue battle directives. If the battle is starting to really degrade I think the remaining players should have the option to go to the "situation room" and see a similar briefing screen to what they saw before, come up with a revised plan, and then resume control of their ships with the updated objectives. 
 ⁃ Game mode combinations: Each game mode can be paired with each combat style. For example, you can do Classic War, Team War, Classic Skirmish, and Team Skirmish. Choosing classic vs team basically just switches whether your squamates control their own airships or if you work together to man one airship chosen from the library of configurations of anyone in the squad
 ⁃ Ship building: I want there to be a very diverse load out of forces you can control. We start off with a tech tree that allows basic airship design with different tradeoffs for armor firepower speed etc. But I want users to also be able to go different routes based on what they want to build, like a big glass cannon ship or a large mothership or even a small fleet of individual little airships that, in "Classic" mode would be controlled similar to how you control troops in games like mount and blade war band (you are in charge of one ship, and give general deployment commands to the others). In "Team" mode, you would all be controlling individual stations
 ⁃ Matchmaking and team comp: This is a big open question. Depending on how the shipbuilding and damage system is implemented, it will be essential to construct teams of an appropriate size for fun combat with a team composition that lends itself to interesting strategy being possible. I think that, based on the attributes of a player's deployed force (single ship or multi-ship) there should be a set of derived statistics about the ship. Then, for matchmaking, we can use an agent to search through the list of queued players and assemble a team. 
 ⁃ Procedural battle generation: Based on some set of rules, the system should procedurally generate a map consisting of obstacles, weather, wildlife hazards, etc. Then, in PvE mode, based on the selected human player team, assemble a commensurate opposing force to make the battle difficult but not impossible to win.

So to summarize, we need to flesh out the following design choices:
 ⁃ Tactical system in pve: how should the plan creation mechanic work, and how should the LLM game masters manage providing players with objectives and moving the game along in a fun way.
 ⁃ Ship driving: how should we handle the ships moving? What motion model balances the fun of high speed with the impact of seeing a capital ship slowly looming on the horizon. How does weather impact this (e.g. strong winds, lightning strikes, rain etc)
 ⁃ Ship ranking: What statistics should we track for ship builds and how should we derive them from a particular build? Based on these statistics, how can we rank vehicles with similar play styles but different components in terms of capability to provide a sense of progression that your ship gets better over time?
 ⁃ Matchmaking: Based on those statistics, what makes a fair team? How can the LLM generate it
 ⁃ Matchmaking speed: Lots of procedural generation goes into each game. How can we decouple the matchmaking queue from the world generation queue? Players should only ever be waiting to be paired with teammates, NOT for their world to be generated AFTER they are paired
 ⁃ Research and money system: How do we determine how much money and research points to assign after battle?
 ⁃ World state: How can we best emulate the engaging world-scale war aspect of helldivers 2? How much should the outcome of 1 battle impact that?
 ⁃ Monetization: How do we make money from this game? Premium components?
 ⁃ Damage system: Obviously we are basing this on war thunder, but transferring that to airships requires some refining
 ⁃ Team mode: Sea of thieves style gameplay is definitely a goal here, but that means that everything about combat has to work for both 3rd person whole ship control and an individual player running around on deck managing guns. This means we need to design all of the systems like gun control, fires, damage model and its impact on ship handling, etc in a way that is the same (uses the same code) for both game modes, just that in team mode individual players are actually within the model and running around and controlling individual components and in classic mode those same individual elements are controlled by a harness that sits on top of the system and exposes simplified controls that lets one person do everything.
 ⁃ Ship building: what are the rules about what is a valid vehicle? I think we can take inspiration from crossout's car building mechanics; the developers of that game also built war thunder and by definition have already figured out the pitfalls of allowing players to build their own vehicles

And come up with specifics for the initial set of elements in the following parts of the game that will then be expanded over time:
 ⁃ Ship parts: what does the initial tech tree look like? What are the categories? What weapons do we start off with
 ⁃ Map elements: clouds, floating rocks and cities, larger floating islands, along with team base for repair
 ⁃ Enemy types: Instead of procedurally generating enemies, it is probably easier to balance a game where we just pre-make a catalog of enemies that can be scaled in attributes or unlock at certain levels and combined to form the enemy team. It will also be faster at matchmaking time
 ⁃ Assets: I'm thinking we should use this asset pack and try to use ModelGen/PrimGen to make similar looking assets: https://kitbash3d.com/products/city-in-the-sky. We can also use these floating island assets as the substrate from which we can procedurally generate the battle maps.
 ⁃ Game lore: I want to flesh the backstory of the world out a little bit.

Future mechanics for the roadmap: 
 ⁃ Ship boarding

answers.ask: How large is a single battle space, and how far apart do the two forces start?
answers.answer: Use a compact battle space sized for a single focused engagement, with opposing forces starting roughly 1–2 minutes of flight apart. This keeps the vertical 3D maneuvering meaningful without long travel downtime.

answers.ask: How much of the fight happens at island level versus in open sky? That decides whether the islands are the map or scenery in it.
answers.answer: The fight is primarily in open sky, with a small number of floating islands, cloud banks, and structures acting as tactical cover, chokepoints, or objective locations. Islands are scenery and combat terrain within the map, not the entire map.

answers.ask: What ends a PvE battle - destroy the enemy force, hold an objective, survive a timer?
answers.answer: PvE battles should end by completing the operation’s staged objectives; these can involve destroying enemy forces, capturing or defending a location, or surviving for a duration. The final objective determines victory rather than requiring every enemy to be destroyed.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How large is a single battle space, and how far apart do the two forces start? A: Use a compact battle space sized for a single focused engagement, with opposing forces starting roughly 1–2 minutes of flight apart. This keeps the vertical 3D maneuvering meaningful without long travel downtime.
- [author] shape — Q: How much of the fight happens at island level versus in open sky? That decides whether the islands are the map or scenery in it. A: The fight is primarily in open sky, with a small number of floating islands, cloud banks, and structures acting as tactical cover, chokepoints, or objective locations. Islands are scenery and combat terrain within the map, not the entire map.
- [author] goal — Q: What ends a PvE battle - destroy the enemy force, hold an objective, survive a timer? A: PvE battles should end by completing the operation’s staged objectives; these can involve destroying enemy forces, capturing or defending a location, or surviving for a duration. The final objective determines victory rather than requiring every enemy to be destroyed.
- [agent_inferred] repair bases — Q: How many repair bases should the initial space contain? A: Use one base for each opposing force at opposite sides so the same initial battlefield supports PvE and PvP; the friendly base contains the planning room.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a compact but fully three-dimensional steampunk-feudal airship battlefield in open sky. Place two opposing repair bases roughly one to two minutes of flight apart, with the friendly base containing an enterable planning and situation room. Between them, distribute a small number of floating islands, larger floating rocks, cloud banks, sky-city structures, and wildlife-threat areas as tactical cover, chokepoints, and candidate objective locations rather than as continuous ground. Arrange several staged-objective sites for attack, capture, defense, or survival operations, and show representative battle airships maneuvering above and between the terrain. Preserve broad vertical flight lanes and clear silhouettes in a single dramatic isometric composition.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Shooter, with Strategy secondary because collaborative planning and staged tactical objectives materially organize the battle space.

## Shape and preset
Use `volume-open-air`, taken from outside Shooter's usual set, because open sky is the primary play volume and islands are discrete terrain within it. It matches the PvE Shooter preset with this shape substitution, retaining hostile origins, chokepoints, and the enterable planning structure.

## Config requirements
Use `spawn-teambase` for the two opposing repair bases, `cover-los` for cloud banks, rocks, and island masses, `choke-bottleneck` for narrow air passes, `building-interior` for the friendly planning room, `island-cluster` for the small number of separated floating landmasses, and `capture-zone` for visible staged-objective sites. Use `tracker-quest`, reached through the shared catalogue from Adventure, for the physical strategy table or briefing wall in the situation room.

## Layout requirements
Place two `spawn-teambase` SpawnZones at opposite repair bases, separated by roughly one to two minutes of flight. Place several candidate `capture-zone` CaptureZones on islands or sky structures, selected per staged operation. Place `spawner-npc` Spawners at the enemy-side approaches and wildlife-threat areas. Place one `tracker-quest` Tracker in the friendly situation room. Matchmaking, objectives, commanders, economy, damage, ship control, and procedural selection are mechanics.

## Layout components
The build contains one volumetric battle space, two opposing repair bases, one linked planning-room interior, a small number of floating islands, cloud banks, floating rocks, sky-city structures, open vertical flight lanes, chokepoints, and several objective sites. Terrain is sparse enough that airships fight primarily in open sky. The flight envelope is the boundary.

## Render order
Render `isometric` first and treat it as authoritative, because vertical airship separation and layered cover cannot be expressed by a single flat plan; verify the resulting play volume for self-occlusion.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use the large scale band because capital airships, bases, and floating terrain must fit while remaining only one to two minutes of flight apart. The theme is steampunk feudal warfare among clouds and sky cities. `CHECK` is required for volumetric open-air play and separated floating islands, and `P3` is required for the exterior battlefield to linked planning-room interior transition.
